chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
Faith (Iman) is acknowledgement and deed, and Islam is acknowledgement without deed.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Iman and Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Ibn Abi Umayr, articulates a key Shia doctrinal distinction where Islam represents the external submission of the tongue, while Iman encompasses both that verbal declaration and internal conviction manifested through righteous deeds. This differentiation underscores the Shia emphasis on the inseparability of belief and practice, contrasting with views that might treat them as entirely distinct entities. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how spiritual status and legal rulings are derived from the interplay of declaration and action.
